title: 028 · Why? #16: the six trig ratios are six real lines (3D; tan θ on the touching line; predict-first; voiced)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Trigonometry. Circle of radius 1. Which line is tan θ? A · B · C 👇

B, the piece of the line that touches the circle. Here's why.
The small triangle has height sin θ and base cos θ. Stretch it from the centre until its base is 1: every side grows by 1/cos θ, so its height becomes sin θ ÷ cos θ = tan θ, standing on the line that touches the circle. That's the name: tangent = touching.
The slant from the centre to it cuts through the circle: sec θ (secant = cutting). Pythagoras: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
Do the same against the line touching the top: cot θ and cosec θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.
Traps: A is sin θ (its triangle's base is cos θ, not 1). C is sec θ.

NDA asked about this in 2024 (II), Q79: lim θ→π/2 (sec θ − tan θ) = ? sec θ − tan θ = (1 − sin θ)/cos θ = cos θ/(1 + sin θ) → 0, so (B) 0. In the picture: as θ grows, both lines shoot up but their gap shrinks.
